sourcing_note: Prompts are written from the author's reading of how a business owner or consultant would ask for each step (anonymised, no client names or figures). Not captured from live runs. Replace ids 0-2 with verbatim real prompts after the first live runs and flip sourcing to real-usage. Until then the build verdict stays SHIP WITH FLAGS.

evals.prompt: Make the new booking app look like our company. Our brand colour is a deep teal and we use a clean sans.
evals.expected_output: Builds tokens.json with light and dark themes and colour roles from the brand teal, runs contrast.py, fixes any FAIL by changing colours, and writes components.md with states.

assertions.text: tokens.json has themes.light and themes.dark each with colors and pairs
Runs scripts/contrast.py and shows the output
Fixes failing pairs by changing the colour, not the minimum

evals.prompt: Just copy the old tool's look so our team feels at home: same colours, same logo style, same icons.
evals.expected_output: Declines to copy the vendor's look: explains the legal risk of reproducing trade dress, logos and icons, and proposes keeping the familiar layout logic while using the business's own palette and icons.

assertions.text: Declines to reuse the vendor's colours, logo or icons
Offers the business's own brand as the alternative
Does not extract the vendor's colour values

evals.prompt: The grey for secondary text is #999 on white. It looks fine to me.
evals.expected_output: Runs the pair through contrast.py, reports it fails the 4.5 minimum for normal text, and proposes a darker grey that passes, rerunning the script.

assertions.text: Reports the ratio from the script, not an estimate
States that it fails the 4.5 minimum
Reruns the script on the fixed value

evals.prompt: Do dark mode later, just ship light for now.
evals.expected_output: Defines both themes now because retrofitting dark mode means redoing every colour pair, and runs contrast on both.

assertions.text: Defines both light and dark themes

evals.prompt: This is a back-end only swap, a nightly sync job with no screens. Do the design step.
evals.expected_output: Says there is no user interface to design, skips the skill, and routes onward to swap-build.

assertions.text: States there is nothing to design
Does not invent screens or tokens
